./agent-references/troubleshooting.md:40:| a watchdog **WARN** (or an escalating streak) fires for a member that is streaming a very long answer — no tool call is open and `session-watchdog-status` shows the step `OUTSTANDING` | **expected, stated on purpose (contract §1 rule 3) — this is the one place where the watchdog is deliberately conservative instead of silent.** An open step stays `OUTSTANDING` until an `assistant/message` / `assistant/attempt` **commits**; while the model is still delivering a long answer nothing is committed, so a step with no first-token signal honestly stays `OUTSTANDING` and has a clock (a COMPLETED step is `ALIVE` forever and has none). The `agent/assistant-stream` **START frame is the ENRICHMENT** that flips the open `(turn,step)` to `ALIVE` (`noteStreamFrame`, `packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/src/channel.ts`; soft-probed at apply): with it unavailable — or with a harness that never emits a first-token signal — `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` is the BOUND that protects instead of silence. Fix: check the enrichment flag in `session-watchdog-status` and raise `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` when answers legitimately run longer, instead of reading the warn as a wedge. The full asymmetry is also in the package README pair (EN + zh-CN). |

./evidence/gates/t75-derived-values/20260917T072029Z/scratch/root/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:570:        block: "//#region mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * R1 dormancy fix: make \"captain silence = DENY\" resolve even for a DORMANT team.\n *\n * The scheduler's expiry tick rides a member IDLE EDGE (`kickMember`), so a team that\n * never kicks again leaves a past-due request `pending` and its requester un-notified.\n * This sweep runs at session start, so the next time anyone works in the workspace the\n * past-due rows resolve and their requesters are told.\n *\n * Registered SEPARATELY from the team policy, and deliberately so: expiry is\n * bookkeeping every session needs, not a feature of auto-routing — it must also run\n * when `sessionTeamPolicy.mode` is `off`. Best-effort: a failure degrades to a warning\n * and can never break or reject a session-start step.\n *\n * Boundary (stated, not implied): expiry is evaluated at EVENTS, never by a timer.\n * The events are \"a member became idle\" (scheduler tick) and \"a session started in\n * this workspace\" (this sweep). A workspace nobody ever opens again resolves nothing.\n * @param ctx - the plugin context (needs `on` and `logger`).\n * @param resolved - the resolved plugin config (provides `stateDir`).\n */\nexport function installInterjectionExpirySweep(ctx, resolved) {\n    ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => {\n        const decision = await next();\n        try {\n            // ONCE PER SESSION, not per step: `agent/pre-step` fires for every step, but\n            // this sweep is a session-start concern (see the sweep guard's declaration).\n            const agentId = payload?.agent?.id;\n            if (typeof agentId === 'string' && agentId !== '') {\n                if (sweptFor.has(agentId))\n                    return decision;\n                sweptFor.add(agentId);\n            }\n            // Resolve the workspace PER CALL from the session that is starting — never a\n            // module-level const and never the process cwd alone (one host serves many\n            // sessions with different workspaces; AGENTS.md §6 State).\n            const workspace = payload?.agent?.session?.header?.cwd ?? process.cwd();\n            const swept = await expireInterjectionsEverywhere(join(workspace, resolved.stateDir));\n            if (swept.expired.length > 0) {\n                ctx.logger.info(`agent-teams: expired ${swept.expired.length} past-due interjection request(s) at session start: ${swept.expired.join(', ')}`);\n            }\n        }\n        catch (error) {\n            ctx.logger.warn(`agent-teams: session-start interjection sweep failed: ${String(error)}`);\n        }\n        return decision;\n    }, { global: true, prepend: true });\n}\n//#endregion mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start",
./evidence/gates/t75-derived-values/20260917T072029Z/scratch/root/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:607:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/** Duplicate window for the R1 delivery-idempotency key (from+to+content). */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DELIVERY_LEASE_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. The window is measured on `ts`, and a record\n * that is already delivered/read is still folded — the point is to stop the ACTION,\n * not to shrink the file; nothing is ever physically deleted.\n * @returns the record that now holds the message (new or folded).\n */\nexport async function appendMailboxDeduped(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, message, options = {}) {\n    const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS;\n    const existing = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    const hit = existing.find((candidate) => messageDedupKey(candidate) === key\n        && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs);\n    if (hit !== undefined) {\n        // R1: the surviving record keeps its OWN delivery/read markers. Dropping them\n        // would clear a live claim (or an acknowledgement) and let a folded duplicate be\n        // delivered again — exactly the duplicate ACTION this primitive exists to stop.\n        const folded = {\n            ...hit,\n            dupCount: (hit.dupCount ?? 1) + 1,\n            ...hit.deliveryClaimedAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveryClaimedAt: hit.deliveryClaimedAt },\n            ...hit.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: hit.deliveredAt },\n            ...hit.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: hit.readAt },\n        };\n        await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [hit.id], () => folded);\n        // `_folded` is a TRANSIENT in-memory marker for the caller (the send boundary must\n        // not re-deliver an already-owned payload). It is never persisted: the record kept\n        // is `folded` alone, so a later fold cannot see a stale marker from an old crash.\n        return { message: { ...folded, _folded: true }, folded: true };\n    }\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 });\n    return { message: { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 }, folded: false };\n}\n/**\n * Clear a mailbox DOWN TO A WATERMARK: every record with `ts <= watermark` is\n * replaced in place by a tombstone, its original bytes are written to an archive\n * sidecar (`inbox/archive/<agentKey>.<watermark>.jsonl` — the recoverable copy), and\n * ONE audit event describes the operation. There is deliberately NO hard-delete\n * branch: the tombstone keeps the id/ts/from/to so the record stays reviewable, and\n * the sidecar makes the cleared bytes recoverable byte-for-byte.\n * @returns the manifest: tombstoned ids, the sidecar path, and the audit event.\n */\nexport async function clearMailboxToWatermark(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, watermark, options = {}) {\n    const messages = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const cleared = messages.filter((message) => message.ts <= watermark && message.tombstone !== true);\n    if (cleared.length === 0) {\n        return { cleared: [], sidecar: undefined, audit: undefined };\n    }\n    const clearedIds = new Set(cleared.map((message) => message.id));\n    // archive-first: the recoverable copy is written AND flushed before the live\n    // file is rewritten, so an interrupted clear always leaves the bytes somewhere.\n    const archiveDir = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', 'archive');\n    await mkdir(archiveDir, { recursive: true });\n    const sidecar = join(archiveDir, `${sanitizeKey(agentKey)}.${watermark}.jsonl`);\n    await atomicWriteText(sidecar, cleared.map((message) => JSON.stringify(message)).join('\\n') + '\\n');\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [...clearedIds], (message) => ({\n        id: message.id,\n        from: message.from,\n        to: message.to,\n        content: '',\n        ts: message.ts,\n        tombstone: true,\n        clearedAt: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n        clearedToWatermark: watermark,\n        archivedTo: sidecar,\n        // R1: PRESERVE the read/delivery markers. Without them a cleared record could\n        // re-open as \"unread\" and be delivered a second time after an acknowledgement.\n        ...message.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: message.readAt },\n        ...message.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: message.deliveredAt },\n        ...message.dupCount === undefined ? {} : { dupCount: message.dupCount },\n    }));\n    const audit = {\n        kind: 'mailbox-cleared',\n        agentKey,\n        watermark,\n        clearedCount: cleared.length,\n        clearedIds: [...clearedIds],\n        sidecar,\n        at: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n    };\n    return { cleared: [...clearedIds], sidecar, audit };\n}\n/**\n * Read only the records that are NOT tombstones (the live view after a clear).\n *\n * TEST-ONLY BY DESIGN (t52, closing review finding F-6). It has no production caller and\n * should not grow one: the scheduler's delivery path composes\n * `deliverableUnread(readUnreadMailbox(...))`, where the tombstone filter is carried\n * INDEPENDENTLY by both `readUnreadMailbox` and `deliverableUnread`, and the claim/ack\n * markers are handled by `claimMailboxDelivery`/`acknowledgeMailbox`. Routing the\n * scheduler through this function instead would drop the lease semantics.\n *\n * It is kept because it is the clearest single-expression statement of the F-3\n * invariant (\"a cleared record is never live again\") and the seam tests assert it\n * directly (`test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs`, `test/t49-send-dedup-wiring.test.mjs`).\n * Deleting it would remove a cheap, direct guard on a defect that has already escaped\n * once, so it stays — explicitly labelled rather than left as an accidental orphan.\n */\nexport async function readLiveMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey) {\n    return (await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey)).filter((message) => message.tombstone !== true);\n}\n/**\n * Enqueue a first-class interjection REQUEST. It is a normal mailbox record with\n * `kind: 'interjection-request'` and `status: 'pending'`, but it lives in its own\n * QUEUE, never in a member's ordinary inbox: the scheduler packs EVERY unread inbox\n * record verbatim and auto-delivers at the next idle edge (lib/scheduler.js:223-228,\n * 287-298), so a request in the normal inbox would be delivered and would BYPASS the\n * captain's approval. The payload carries summary + reason + location only; the body\n * follows only after approval.\n *\n * FIELD CONTRACT (repair V1). The mailbox shape REQUIRES a non-empty `content`\n * string, and a record that fails the shape check is invisible to every reader —\n * which used to let a caller create a request that returned `status:'pending'` while\n * nobody could ever see or decide it (a silent failure). `content` is therefore\n * NORMALIZED here rather than left optional: when the caller omits it (or passes an\n * empty string) it is derived, in this fixed priority order, from\n * `summary` -> `reason` -> `location`. `id`, `from` and `ts` are REQUIRED and are\n * rejected loudly when missing, because no fallback can invent an identity or a clock.\n * @param request - the request; `id`/`from`/`ts` required, `content` optional (normalized).\n * @returns the queued request record (always carrying a readable `content`).\n * @throws when a required identity field is missing, naming the field.\n */\nexport async function enqueueInterjection(stateRoot, teamId, request) {\n    for (const field of ['id', 'from', 'ts']) {\n        const value = request?.[field];\n        if (value === undefined || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '')) {\n            throw new Error(`interjection request is missing required field \"${field}\"`);\n        }\n    }\n    // Same fixed priority as the doc above; the first non-empty candidate wins.\n    const rawContent = typeof request.content === 'string' ? request.content.trim() : '';\n    const content = rawContent !== ''\n        ? request.content\n        : (typeof request.summary === 'string' && request.summary.trim() !== ''\n            ? request.summary\n            : (typeof request.reason === 'string' && request.reason.trim() !== ''\n                ? request.reason\n                : (typeof request.location === 'string' ? request.location : '')));\n    const record = {\n        ...request,\n        id: request.id,\n        from: request.from,\n        content,\n        to: INTERJECTION_QUEUE,\n        kind: INTERJECTION_KIND,\n        status: 'pending',\n        ts: request.ts,\n        expiresAt: request.ts + INTERJECTION_TTL_MS,\n    };\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE, record);\n    return record;\n}\n/**\n * Every line of the interjection queue that parses as JSON, WITHOUT the mailbox shape\n * check. This is how a MALFORMED record (present on disk, unreadable by the normal\n * reader) is told apart from a record that truly does not exist.\n */\nasync function readRawInterjectionRecords(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    const file = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', `${sanitizeKey(INTERJECTION_QUEUE)}.jsonl`);\n    let raw;\n    try {\n        raw = await readFile(file, 'utf8');\n    }\n    catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof Error && 'code' in error && error.code === 'ENOENT')\n            return [];\n        throw error;\n    }\n    const records = [];\n    for (const rawLine of raw.split('\\n')) {\n        const line = stripLeadingBom(rawLine);\n        if (line.trim() === '')\n            continue;\n        try {\n            records.push(JSON.parse(line));\n        }\n        catch {\n            // a non-JSON line cannot carry an id; it is reported by the reader's hook\n        }\n    }\n    return records;\n}\n/** Every interjection request in one state, newest last. */\nexport async function readInterjections(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    return readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE);\n}\n/**\n * Read interjections that are still AWAITING DECISION. This is the function the\n * scheduler must use instead of a blanket unread scan: pending requests are never\n * auto-delivered.\n */\nexport async function readPendingInterjections(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    return (await readInterjections(stateRoot, teamId)).filter((record) => record.status === 'pending');\n}\n/**\n * Expire every pending interjection whose TTL has passed: captain silence is a\n * DEFAULT DENY, and the requesting member is notified (status `expired`).\n * @returns the expired ids.\n */\nexport async function expireInterjections(stateRoot, teamId, options = {}) {\n    const now = options.now ?? Date.now();\n    const pending = await readPendingInterjections(stateRoot, teamId);\n    const expired = pending.filter((record) => typeof record.expiresAt === 'number' && record.expiresAt <= now);\n    if (expired.length === 0)\n        return [];\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE, expired.map((record) => record.id), (record) => ({ ...record, status: 'expired', decidedAt: now }));\n    // R1: silence is a DEFAULT DENY, and the requester must be TOLD. The notice is an\n    // ORDINARY message (no interjection kind), so it travels the normal delivery path\n    // and cannot be filtered out by the interjection gate.\n    for (const record of expired) {\n        if (typeof record.from !== 'string' || record.from === '')\n            continue;\n        await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, record.from, {\n            ...createExpiryNotice(record),\n            id: `interjection-expired-${record.id}`,\n            from: CAPTAIN_KEY,\n            to: record.from,\n            ts: now,\n        });\n    }\n    return expired.map((record) => record.id);\n}\n/** The ordinary notice a requester receives when their interjection request expires. */\nfunction createExpiryNotice(record) {\n    const receivedAt = typeof record.ts === 'number' ? new Date(record.ts).toISOString() : '(unknown time)';\n    return {\n        content: `Your interjection request \"${String(record.id)}\" (sent ${receivedAt}) EXPIRED without a captain decision, so it is denied by default. It was not delivered to anyone.`,\n    };\n}\n/** Record the captain's decision on one interjection request. */\nexport async function decideInterjection(stateRoot, teamId, interjectionId, decision, options = {}) {\n    const now = options.now ?? Date.now();\n    const record = (await readInterjections(stateRoot, teamId)).find((candidate) => candidate.id === interjectionId);\n    if (record === undefined) {\n        // Repair V1: a record that IS on disk but fails the mailbox shape check is\n        // MALFORMED, not absent. Reporting it as \"does not exist\" hid the real cause\n        // and sent the caller hunting for a wrong id.\n        const present = (await readRawInterjectionRecords(stateRoot, teamId)).some((candidate) => candidate?.id === interjectionId);\n        if (present) {\n            throw new Error(`interjection \"${interjectionId}\" exists but is MALFORMED (present in the queue but not readable: the mailbox shape requires a non-empty string content and the identity fields); re-enqueue it with content, or inspect the queue file`);\n        }\n        throw new Error(`interjection \"${interjectionId}\" does not exist`);\n    }\n    if (record.status !== 'pending')\n        throw new Error(`interjection \"${interjectionId}\" is already ${String(record.status)}`);\n    // R1: the decision vocabulary is CLOSED. Anything else is a caller bug and must be\n    // named loudly instead of being persisted as an unknown status.\n    const ALLOWED_INTERJECTION_DECISIONS = ['approved', 'rejected'];\n    if (!ALLOWED_INTERJECTION_DECISIONS.includes(decision)) {\n        throw new Error(`invalid interjection decision \"${String(decision)}\"; allowed values are: ${ALLOWED_INTERJECTION_DECISIONS.join(', ')}`);\n    }\n    const decided = { ...record, status: decision, decidedAt: now };\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE, [interjectionId], () => decided);\n    // R1 \"delivery after approval\": the APPROVED body is re-posted as an ORDINARY message\n    // in the requester's inbox. It therefore rides the existing member-prompt queue seam\n    // at the next step boundary like any other mailbox work — the plugin never calls the\n    // harness sendMessage/steer path for team work (AGENTS.md §12), and the requester's\n    // running attempt is not restarted (frozen S4).\n    if (decision === 'approved' && typeof record.from === 'string' && record.from !== '') {\n        const body = typeof options.body === 'string' && options.body !== ''\n            ? options.body\n            : (typeof record.body === 'string' && record.body !== '' ? record.body : record.content);\n        await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, record.from, {\n            id: `${interjectionId}-delivery`,\n            from: options.captainKey ?? CAPTAIN_KEY,\n            to: record.from,\n            content: `Approved interjection \"${interjectionId}\": ${body}`,\n            ts: now,\n        });\n    }\n    return decided;\n}\n//#endregion mpd-delta message-channel-r1",

./evidence/gates/t75-derived-values/20260917T072029Z/after-index-fix/root/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:607:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/** Duplicate window for the R1 delivery-idempotency key (from+to+content). */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DELIVERY_LEASE_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. The window is measured on `ts`, and a record\n * that is already delivered/read is still folded — the point is to stop the ACTION,\n * not to shrink the file; nothing is ever physically deleted.\n * @returns the record that now holds the message (new or folded).\n */\nexport async function appendMailboxDeduped(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, message, options = {}) {\n    const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? Dropping them\n        // would clear a live claim (or an acknowledgement) and let a folded duplicate be\n        // delivered again — exactly the duplicate ACTION this primitive exists to stop.\n        const folded = {\n            ...hit,\n            dupCount: (hit.dupCount ?? 1) + 1,\n            ...hit.deliveryClaimedAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveryClaimedAt: hit.deliveryClaimedAt },\n            ...hit.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: hit.deliveredAt },\n            ...hit.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: hit.readAt },\n        };\n        await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [hit.id], () => folded);\n        // `_folded` is a TRANSIENT in-memory marker for the caller (the send boundary must\n        // not re-deliver an already-owned payload). Date.now(),\n        clearedToWatermark: watermark,\n        archivedTo: sidecar,\n        // R1: PRESERVE the read/delivery markers. Without them a cleared record could\n        // re-open as \"unread\" and be delivered a second time after an acknowledgement.\n        ...message.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: message.readAt },\n        ...message.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: message.deliveredAt },\n        ...message.dupCount === undefined ? {} : { dupCount: message.dupCount },\n    }));\n    const audit = {\n        kind: 'mailbox-cleared',\n        agentKey,\n        watermark,\n        clearedCount: cleared.length,\n        clearedIds: [...clearedIds],\n        sidecar,\n        at: options.now ?? ./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-09-17T07-39-32.206Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/agent-references/troubleshooting.md:40:| a watchdog **WARN** (or an escalating streak) fires for a member that is streaming a very long answer — no tool call is open and `session-watchdog-status` shows the step `OUTSTANDING` | **expected, stated on purpose (contract §1 rule 3) — this is the one place where the watchdog is deliberately conservative instead of silent.** An open step stays `OUTSTANDING` until an `assistant/message` / `assistant/attempt` **commits**; while the model is still delivering a long answer nothing is committed, so a step with no first-token signal honestly stays `OUTSTANDING` and has a clock (a COMPLETED step is `ALIVE` forever and has none). The `agent/assistant-stream` **START frame is the ENRICHMENT** that flips the open `(turn,step)` to `ALIVE` (`noteStreamFrame`, `packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/src/channel.ts`; soft-probed at apply): with it unavailable — or with a harness that never emits a first-token signal — `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` is the BOUND that protects instead of silence. Fix: check the enrichment flag in `session-watchdog-status` and raise `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` when answers legitimately run longer, instead of reading the warn as a wedge. ./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-10-04T04-08-19.501Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:1170:        block: "//#region mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * R1 dormancy fix: make \"captain silence = DENY\" resolve even for a DORMANT team.\n *\n * The scheduler's expiry tick rides a member IDLE EDGE (`kickMember`), so a team that\n * never kicks again leaves a past-due request `pending` and its requester un-notified.\n * This sweep runs at session start, so the next time anyone works in the workspace the\n * past-due rows resolve and their requesters are told.\n *\n * Registered SEPARATELY from the team policy, and deliberately so: expiry is\n * bookkeeping every session needs, not a feature of auto-routing — it must also run\n * when `sessionTeamPolicy.mode` is `off`. Best-effort: a failure degrades to a warning\n * and can never break or reject a session-start step.\n *\n * Boundary (stated, not implied): expiry is evaluated at EVENTS, never by a timer.\n * The events are \"a member became idle\" (scheduler tick) and \"a session started in\n * this workspace\" (this sweep). A workspace nobody ever opens again resolves nothing.\n * @param ctx - the plugin context (needs `on` and `logger`).\n * @param resolved - the resolved plugin config (provides `stateDir`).\n */\nexport function installInterjectionExpirySweep(ctx, resolved) {\n    ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => {\n        const decision = await next();\n        try {\n            // ONCE PER SESSION, not per step: `agent/pre-step` fires for every step, but\n            // this sweep is a session-start concern (see the sweep guard's declaration).\n            const agentId = payload?.agent?.id;\n            if (typeof agentId === 'string' && agentId !== '') {\n                if (sweptFor.has(agentId))\n                    return decision;\n                sweptFor.add(agentId);\n            }\n            // Resolve the workspace PER CALL from the session that is starting — never a\n            // module-level const and never the process cwd alone (one host serves many\n            // sessions with different workspaces; AGENTS.md §6 State).\n            const workspace = payload?.agent?.session?.header?.cwd ?? process.cwd();\n            const swept = await expireInterjectionsEverywhere(join(workspace, resolved.stateDir));\n            if (swept.expired.length > 0) {\n                ctx.logger.info(`agent-teams: expired ${swept.expired.length} past-due interjection request(s) at session start: ${swept.expired.join(', ')}`);\n            }\n        }\n        catch (error) {\n            ctx.logger.warn(`agent-teams: session-start interjection sweep failed: ${String(error)}`);\n        }\n        return decision;\n    }, { global: true, prepend: true });\n}\n//#endregion mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start",
./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-10-04T04-08-19.501Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:1265:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * P1e (t47): the duplicate window is a CONFIGURED value with its own default, NOT the delivery lease\n * constant it used to borrow. MEASURED basis: the lease is 60 s, while the exact-repeat groups this\n * mailbox actually produced sit at a median of 43.3 s and a maximum of 1,131.6 s — so the borrowed\n * constant could only see 4 of 7, and across every team and archive 2,084 records carry `dupCount`\n * with EVERY value 1, i.e. no fold has ever happened. 30 min covers all seven; `0` (or any\n * non-positive value) DISABLES the fold — proven by an arm, not by this sentence.\n */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/**\n * P1b (t49): the retention window for the AUTOMATIC prune. MEASURED justification for 7 days: the\n * longest exact-repeat gap this mailbox ever produced is 1,131.6 s (19 min) and the dedup window is\n * 30 min, so a week is ~500x beyond any evidence the fold could still need; meanwhile the workspace\n * holds 116 inbox files / 3,302 records (largest 1.0 MB / 410 records) with NO automatic tombstone\n * ever created — so the window is long enough to keep anything reviewable and short enough to\n * actually reclaim. 0 disables the prune (proven by an arm).\n */\nexport const MAILBOX_RETENTION_DEFAULT_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n/** How many records one bounded prune may reclaim (the sweep never becomes a scan of the mailbox). */\nexport const MAILBOX_RETENTION_BATCH = 64;\n/** Back-compat alias: the default window, no longer the lease constant. */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * P1d (t48): every existing record a message would REPEAT — same identity, same recipient, same\n * content — at ANY age. The fold window decides FOLDABILITY, never VISIBILITY: a sender must be able\n * to see a repeat from three days ago, which is the whole point of the pre-send gate. Cleared\n * tombstones are not repeats (their content is empty by construction).\n */\nexport function mailboxDuplicatesFor(existing, message, windowMs) {\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    return (existing ?? [])\n        .filter((candidate) => candidate.tombstone !== true && messageDedupKey(candidate) === key)\n        .map((candidate) => ({\n            id: candidate.id,\n            ts: candidate.ts,\n            dup_count: candidate.dupCount ?? 1,\n            within_fold_window: Number.isFinite(windowMs) && windowMs > 0 && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs,\n        }))\n        .sort((left, right) => right.ts - left.ts);\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. The window is measured on `ts`, and a record\n * that is already delivered/read is still folded — the point is to stop the ACTION,\n * not to shrink the file; nothing is ever physically deleted.\n * @returns the record that now holds the message (new or folded).\n */\nexport async function appendMailboxDeduped(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, message, options = {}) {\n    // P1e: `windowMs <= 0` is OFF — a configured 0 must fold NOTHING, not \"fold only same-millisecond\n    // records\", which is what `Math.abs(...) <= 0` would have meant.\n    const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS;\n    const foldable = Number.isFinite(windowMs) && windowMs > 0;\n    const existing = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    const hit = foldable\n        ? existing.find((candidate) => messageDedupKey(candidate) === key\n            && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs)\n        : undefined;\n    if (hit !== undefined) {\n        // R1: the surviving record keeps its OWN delivery/read markers. Dropping them\n        // would clear a live claim (or an acknowledgement) and let a folded duplicate be\n        // delivered again — exactly the duplicate ACTION this primitive exists to stop.\n        const folded = {\n            ...hit,\n            dupCount: (hit.dupCount ?? 1) + 1,\n            ...hit.deliveryClaimedAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveryClaimedAt: hit.deliveryClaimedAt },\n            ...hit.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: hit.deliveredAt },\n            ...hit.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: hit.readAt },\n        };\n        await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [hit.id], () => folded);\n        // `_folded` is a TRANSIENT in-memory marker for the caller (the send boundary must\n        // not re-deliver an already-owned payload). It is never persisted: the record kept\n        // is `folded` alone, so a later fold cannot see a stale marker from an old crash.\n        return { message: { ...folded, _folded: true }, folded: true };\n    }\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 });\n    return { message: { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 }, folded: false };\n}\n/**\n * Clear a mailbox DOWN TO A WATERMARK: every record with `ts <= watermark` is\n * replaced in place by a tombstone, its original bytes are written to an archive\n * sidecar (`inbox/archive/<agentKey>.<watermark>.jsonl` — the recoverable copy), and\n * ONE audit event describes the operation. There is deliberately NO hard-delete\n * branch: the tombstone keeps the id/ts/from/to so the record stays reviewable, and\n * the sidecar makes the cleared bytes recoverable byte-for-byte.\n * @returns the manifest: tombstoned ids, the sidecar path, and the audit event.\n */\nexport async function clearMailboxToWatermark(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, watermark, options = {}) {\n    const messages = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const inScope = messages.filter((message) => message.ts <= watermark && message.tombstone !== true);\n    // P1c (t43, the user's directive): a WATERMARK alone can silently destroy undelivered work — the\n    // measured instance is the captain's own `9999999999999` call, which tombstoned a member's entire\n    // delivery view (162 records, 0 live) while the tool reported FAILURE. A record that was never\n    // DELIVERED or never READ is therefore PROTECTED unless the caller passes `force: true`, and the\n    // split is REPORTED so the caller sees what it was about to lose. The sidecar is what keeps the\n    // operation recoverable, and this guard is what keeps it from being unnecessary.\n    const protectedRecords = inScope.filter((message) => message.deliveredAt === undefined || message.readAt === undefined);\n    const forced = options.force === true;\n    const cleared = forced ? inScope : inScope.filter((message) => !protectedRecords.includes(message));\n    const skipped = forced ? [] : protectedRecords.map((message) => message.id);\n    if (cleared.length === 0) {\n        return { cleared: [], skipped_unread: skipped, sidecar: undefined, audit: undefined };\n    }\n    const clearedIds = new Set(cleared.map((message) => message.id));\n    // archive-first: the recoverable copy is written AND flushed before the live\n    // file is rewritten, so an interrupted clear always leaves the bytes somewhere.\n    const archiveDir = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', 'archive');\n    await mkdir(archiveDir, { recursive: true });\n    const sidecar = join(archiveDir, `${sanitizeKey(agentKey)}.${watermark}.jsonl`);\n    await atomicWriteText(sidecar, cleared.map((message) => JSON.stringify(message)).join('\\n') + '\\n');\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [...clearedIds], (message) => ({\n        id: message.id,\n        from: message.from,\n        to: message.to,\n        content: '',\n        ts: message.ts,\n        tombstone: true,\n        clearedAt: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n        clearedToWatermark: watermark,\n        archivedTo: sidecar,\n        // R1: PRESERVE the read/delivery markers. Without them a cleared record could\n        // re-open as \"unread\" and be delivered a second time after an acknowledgement.\n        ...message.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: message.readAt },\n        ...message.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: message.deliveredAt },\n        ...message.dupCount === undefined ? {} : { dupCount: message.dupCount },\n    }));\n    const audit = {\n        kind: 'mailbox-cleared',\n        agentKey,\n        watermark,\n        clearedCount: cleared.length,\n        skippedUnreadCount: skipped.length,\n        clearedIds: [...clearedIds],\n        sidecar,\n        at: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n    };\n    return { cleared: [...clearedIds], skipped_unread: skipped, sidecar, audit };\n}\n/**\n * Read only the records that are NOT tombstones (the live view after a clear).\n *\n * TEST-ONLY BY DESIGN (t52, closing review finding F-6). It has no production caller and\n * should not grow one: the scheduler's delivery path composes\n * `deliverableUnread(readUnreadMailbox(...))`, where the tombstone filter is carried\n * INDEPENDENTLY by both `readUnreadMailbox` and `deliverableUnread`, and the claim/ack\n * markers are handled by `claimMailboxDelivery`/`acknowledgeMailbox`. Routing the\n * scheduler through this function instead would drop the lease semantics.\n *\n * It is kept because it is the clearest single-expression statement of the F-3\n * invariant (\"a cleared record is never live again\") and the seam tests assert it\n * directly (`test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs`, `test/t49-send-dedup-wiring.test.mjs`).\n * Deleting it would remove a cheap, direct guard on a defect that has already escaped\n * once, so it stays — explicitly labelled rather than left as an accidental orphan.\n */\nexport async function readLiveMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey) {\n    return (await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey)).filter((message) => message.tombstone !== true);\n}\n/**\n * Enqueue a first-class interjection REQUEST. It is a normal mailbox record with\n * `kind: 'interjection-request'` and `status: 'pending'`, but it lives in its own\n * QUEUE, never in a member's ordinary inbox: the scheduler packs EVERY unread inbox\n * record verbatim and auto-delivers at the next idle edge (lib/scheduler.ts:223-228,\n * 287-298), so a request in the normal inbox would be delivered and would BYPASS the\n * captain's approval. The payload carries summary + reason + location only; the body\n * follows only after approval.\n *\n * FIELD CONTRACT (repair V1). The mailbox shape REQUIRES a non-empty `content`\n * string, and a record that fails the shape check is invisible to every reader —\n * which used to let a caller create a request that returned `status:'pending'` while\n * nobody could ever see or decide it (a silent failure). `content` is therefore\n * NORMALIZED here rather than left optional: when the caller omits it (or passes an\n * empty string) it is derived, in this fixed priority order, from\n * `summary` -> `reason` -> `location`. `id`, `from` and `ts` are REQUIRED and are\n * rejected loudly when missing, because no fallback can invent an identity or a clock.\n * @param request - the request; `id`/`from`/`ts` required, `content` optional (normalized).\n * @returns the queued request record (always carrying a readable `content`).\n * @throws when a required identity field is missing, naming the field.\n */\nexport async function enqueueInterjection(stateRoot, teamId, request) {\n    for (const field of ['id', 'from', 'ts']) {\n        const value = request?.[field];\n        if (value === undefined || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '')) {\n            throw new Error(`interjection request is missing required field \"${field}\"`);\n        }\n    }\n    // Same fixed priority as the doc above; the first non-empty candidate wins.\n    const rawContent = typeof request.content === 'string' ? request.content.trim() : '';\n    const content = rawContent !== ''\n        ? request.content\n        : (typeof request.summary === 'string' && request.summary.trim() !== ''\n            ? request.summary\n            : (typeof request.reason === 'string' && request.reason.trim() !== ''\n                ? request.reason\n                : (typeof request.location === 'string' ? request.location : '')));\n    const record = {\n        ...request,\n        id: request.id,\n        from: request.from,\n        content,\n        to: INTERJECTION_QUEUE,\n        kind: INTERJECTION_KIND,\n        status: 'pending',\n        ts: request.ts,\n        expiresAt: request.ts + INTERJECTION_TTL_MS,\n    };\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE, record);\n    return record;\n}\n/**\n * Every line of the interjection queue that parses as JSON, WITHOUT the mailbox shape\n * check. This is how a MALFORMED record (present on disk, unreadable by the normal\n * reader) is told apart from a record that truly does not exist.\n */\nasync function readRawInterjectionRecords(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    const file = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', `${sanitizeKey(INTERJECTION_QUEUE)}.jsonl`);\n    let raw;\n    try {\n        raw = await readFile(file, 'utf8');\n    }\n    catch (error) {\n        if (error instanceof Error && 'code' in error && error.code === 'ENOENT')\n            return [];\n        throw error;\n    }\n    const records = [];\n    for (const rawLine of raw.split('\\n')) {\n        const line = stripLeadingBom(rawLine);\n        if (line.trim() === '')\n            continue;\n        try {\n            records.push(JSON.parse(line));\n        }\n        catch {\n            // a non-JSON line cannot carry an id; it is reported by the reader's hook\n        }\n    }\n    return records;\n}\n/** Every interjection request in one state, newest last. */\nexport async function readInterjections(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    return readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE);\n}\n/**\n * Read interjections that are still AWAITING DECISION. This is the function the\n * scheduler must use instead of a blanket unread scan: pending requests are never\n * auto-delivered.\n */\nexport async function readPendingInterjections(stateRoot, teamId) {\n    return (await readInterjections(stateRoot, teamId)).filter((record) => record.status === 'pending');\n}\n/**\n * Expire every pending interjection whose TTL has passed: captain silence is a\n * DEFAULT DENY, and the requesting member is notified (status `expired`).\n * @returns the expired ids.\n */\nexport async function expireInterjections(stateRoot, teamId, options = {}) {\n    const now = options.now ?? Date.now();\n    const pending = await readPendingInterjections(stateRoot, teamId);\n    const expired = pending.filter((record) => typeof record.expiresAt === 'number' && record.expiresAt <= now);\n    if (expired.length === 0)\n        return [];\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, INTERJECTION_QUEUE, expired.map((record) => record.id), (record) => ({ ...record, status: 'expired', decidedAt: now }));\n    // R1: silence is a DEFAULT DENY, and the requester must be TOLD. The notice is an\n    // ORDINARY message (no interjection kind), so it travels the normal delivery path\n    // and cannot be filtered out by the interjection gate.\n    for (const record of expired) {\n        if (typeof record.from !== 'string' || record.from === '')\n            continue;\n        await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, record.from, {\n            ...createExpiryNotice(record),\n            id: `interjection-expired-${record.id}`,\n            from: CAPTAIN_KEY,\n            to: record.from,\n            ts: now,\n        });\n    }\n    return expired.map((record) => record.id);\n}\n/** The ordinary notice a requester receives when their interjection request expires. */\nfunction createExpiryNotice(record) {\n    const receivedAt = typeof record.ts === 'number' ? new Date(record.ts).toISOString() : '(unknown time)';\n    return {\n        content: `Your interjection request \"${String(record.id)}\" (sent ${receivedAt}) EXPIRED without a captain decision, so it is denied by default. ./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-10-06T02-50-11.088Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:1170:        block: "//#region mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * R1 dormancy fix: make \"captain silence = DENY\" resolve even for a DORMANT team.\n *\n * The scheduler's expiry tick rides a member IDLE EDGE (`kickMember`), so a team that\n * never kicks again leaves a past-due request `pending` and its requester un-notified.\n * This sweep runs at session start, so the next time anyone works in the workspace the\n * past-due rows resolve and their requesters are told.\n *\n * Registered SEPARATELY from the team policy, and deliberately so: expiry is\n * bookkeeping every session needs, not a feature of auto-routing — it must also run\n * when `sessionTeamPolicy.mode` is `off`. Best-effort: a failure degrades to a warning\n * and can never break or reject a session-start step.\n *\n * Boundary (stated, not implied): expiry is evaluated at EVENTS, never by a timer.\n * The events are \"a member became idle\" (scheduler tick) and \"a session started in\n * this workspace\" (this sweep). A workspace nobody ever opens again resolves nothing.\n * @param ctx - the plugin context (needs `on` and `logger`).\n * @param resolved - the resolved plugin config (provides `stateDir`).\n */\nexport function installInterjectionExpirySweep(ctx, resolved) {\n    ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => {\n        const decision = await next();\n        try {\n            // ONCE PER SESSION, not per step: `agent/pre-step` fires for every step, but\n            // this sweep is a session-start concern (see the sweep guard's declaration).\n            const agentId = payload?.agent?.id;\n            if (typeof agentId === 'string' && agentId !== '') {\n                if (sweptFor.has(agentId))\n                    return decision;\n                sweptFor.add(agentId);\n            }\n            // Resolve the workspace PER CALL from the session that is starting — never a\n            // module-level const and never the process cwd alone (one host serves many\n            // sessions with different workspaces; AGENTS.md §6 State).\n            const workspace = payload?.agent?.session?.header?.cwd ?? process.cwd();\n            const swept = await expireInterjectionsEverywhere(join(workspace, resolved.stateDir));\n            if (swept.expired.length > 0) {\n                ctx.logger.info(`agent-teams: expired ${swept.expired.length} past-due interjection request(s) at session start: ${swept.expired.join(', ')}`);\n            }\n        }\n        catch (error) {\n            ctx.logger.warn(`agent-teams: session-start interjection sweep failed: ${String(error)}`);\n        }\n        return decision;\n    }, { global: true, prepend: true });\n}\n//#endregion mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start",
./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-10-06T02-50-11.088Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:1265:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * P1e (t47): the duplicate window is a CONFIGURED value with its own default, NOT the delivery lease\n * constant it used to borrow. MEASURED basis: the lease is 60 s, while the exact-repeat groups this\n * mailbox actually produced sit at a median of 43.3 s and a maximum of 1,131.6 s — so the borrowed\n * constant could only see 4 of 7, and across every team and archive 2,084 records carry `dupCount`\n * with EVERY value 1, i.e. no fold has ever happened. 30 min covers all seven; `0` (or any\n * non-positive value) DISABLES the fold — proven by an arm, not by this sentence.\n */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/**\n * P1b (t49): the retention window for the AUTOMATIC prune. MEASURED justification for 7 days: the\n * longest exact-repeat gap this mailbox ever produced is 1,131.6 s (19 min) and the dedup window is\n * 30 min, so a week is ~500x beyond any evidence the fold could still need; meanwhile the workspace\n * holds 116 inbox files / 3,302 records (largest 1.0 MB / 410 records) with NO automatic tombstone\n * ever created — so the window is long enough to keep anything reviewable and short enough to\n * actually reclaim. 0 disables the prune (proven by an arm).\n */\nexport const MAILBOX_RETENTION_DEFAULT_MS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;\n/** How many records one bounded prune may reclaim (the sweep never becomes a scan of the mailbox). */\nexport const MAILBOX_RETENTION_BATCH = 64;\n/** Back-compat alias: the default window, no longer the lease constant. */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * P1d (t48): every existing record a message would REPEAT — same identity, same recipient, same\n * content — at ANY age. The fold window decides FOLDABILITY, never VISIBILITY: a sender must be able\n * to see a repeat from three days ago, which is the whole point of the pre-send gate. Cleared\n * tombstones are not repeats (their content is empty by construction).\n */\nexport function mailboxDuplicatesFor(existing, message, windowMs) {\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    return (existing ?? [])\n        .filter((candidate) => candidate.tombstone !== true && messageDedupKey(candidate) === key)\n        .map((candidate) => ({\n            id: candidate.id,\n            ts: candidate.ts,\n            dup_count: candidate.dupCount ?? 1,\n            within_fold_window: Number.isFinite(windowMs) && windowMs > 0 && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs,\n        }))\n        .sort((left, right) => right.ts - left.ts);\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. The window is measured on `ts`, and a record\n * that is already delivered/read is still folded — the point is to stop the ACTION,\n * not to shrink the file; nothing is ever physically deleted.\n * @returns the record that now holds the message (new or folded).\n */\nexport async function appendMailboxDeduped(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, message, options = {}) {\n    // P1e: `windowMs <= 0` is OFF — a configured 0 must fold NOTHING, not \"fold only same-millisecond\n    // records\", which is what `Math.abs(...) <= 0` would have meant.\n    const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_DEFAULT_MS;\n    const foldable = Number.isFinite(windowMs) && windowMs > 0;\n    const existing = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    const hit = foldable\n        ? existing.find((candidate) => messageDedupKey(candidate) === key\n            && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs)\n        : undefined;\n    if (hit !== undefined) {\n        // R1: the surviving record keeps its OWN delivery/read markers. Dropping them\n        // would clear a live claim (or an acknowledgement) and let a folded duplicate be\n        // delivered again — exactly the duplicate ACTION this primitive exists to stop.\n        const folded = {\n            ...hit,\n            dupCount: (hit.dupCount ?? 1) + 1,\n            ...hit.deliveryClaimedAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveryClaimedAt: hit.deliveryClaimedAt },\n            ...hit.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: hit.deliveredAt },\n            ...hit.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: hit.readAt },\n        };\n        await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [hit.id], () => folded);\n        // `_folded` is a TRANSIENT in-memory marker for the caller (the send boundary must\n        // not re-deliver an already-owned payload). It is never persisted: the record kept\n        // is `folded` alone, so a later fold cannot see a stale marker from an old crash.\n        return { message: { ...folded, _folded: true }, folded: true };\n    }\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 });\n    return { message: { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 }, folded: false };\n}\n/**\n * Clear a mailbox DOWN TO A WATERMARK: every record with `ts <= watermark` is\n * replaced in place by a tombstone, its original bytes are written to an archive\n * sidecar (`inbox/archive/<agentKey>.<watermark>.jsonl` — the recoverable copy), and\n * ONE audit event describes the operation. There is deliberately NO hard-delete\n * branch: the tombstone keeps the id/ts/from/to so the record stays reviewable, and\n * the sidecar makes the cleared bytes recoverable byte-for-byte.\n * @returns the manifest: tombstoned ids, the sidecar path, and the audit event.\n */\nexport async function clearMailboxToWatermark(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, watermark, options = {}) {\n    const messages = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const inScope = messages.filter((message) => message.ts <= watermark && message.tombstone !== true);\n    // P1c (t43, the user's directive): a WATERMARK alone can silently destroy undelivered work — the\n    // measured instance is the captain's own `9999999999999` call, which tombstoned a member's entire\n    // delivery view (162 records, 0 live) while the tool reported FAILURE. A record that was never\n    // DELIVERED or never READ is therefore PROTECTED unless the caller passes `force: true`, and the\n    // split is REPORTED so the caller sees what it was about to lose. The sidecar is what keeps the\n    // operation recoverable, and this guard is what keeps it from being unnecessary.\n    const protectedRecords = inScope.filter((message) => message.deliveredAt === undefined || message.readAt === undefined);\n    const forced = options.force === true;\n    const cleared = forced ? inScope : inScope.filter((message) => !protectedRecords.includes(message));\n    const skipped = forced ? [] : protectedRecords.map((message) => message.id);\n    if (cleared.length === 0) {\n        return { cleared: [], skipped_unread: skipped, sidecar: undefined, audit: undefined };\n    }\n    const clearedIds = new Set(cleared.map((message) => message.id));\n    // archive-first: the recoverable copy is written AND flushed before the live\n    // file is rewritten, so an interrupted clear always leaves the bytes somewhere.\n    const archiveDir = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', 'archive');\n    await mkdir(archiveDir, { recursive: true });\n    const sidecar = join(archiveDir, `${sanitizeKey(agentKey)}.${watermark}.jsonl`);\n    await atomicWriteText(sidecar, cleared.map((message) => JSON.stringify(message)).join('\\n') + '\\n');\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [...clearedIds], (message) => ({\n        id: message.id,\n        from: message.from,\n        to: message.to,\n        content: '',\n        ts: message.ts,\n        tombstone: true,\n        clearedAt: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n        clearedToWatermark: watermark,\n        archivedTo: sidecar,\n        // R1: PRESERVE the read/delivery markers. Without them a cleared record could\n        // re-open as \"unread\" and be delivered a second time after an acknowledgement.\n        ...message.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: message.readAt },\n        ...message.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: message.deliveredAt },\n        ...message.dupCount === undefined ? {} : { dupCount: message.dupCount },\n    }));\n    const audit = {\n        kind: 'mailbox-cleared',\n        agentKey,\n        watermark,\n        clearedCount: cleared.length,\n        skippedUnreadCount: skipped.length,\n        clearedIds: [...clearedIds],\n        sidecar,\n        at: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n    };\n    return { cleared: [...clearedIds], skipped_unread: skipped, sidecar, audit };\n}\n/**\n * Read only the records that are NOT tombstones (the live view after a clear).\n *\n * TEST-ONLY BY DESIGN (t52, closing review finding F-6). It has no production caller and\n * should not grow one: the scheduler's delivery path composes\n * `deliverableUnread(readUnreadMailbox(...))`, where the tombstone filter is carried\n * INDEPENDENTLY by both `readUnreadMailbox` and `deliverableUnread`, and the claim/ack\n * markers are handled by `claimMailboxDelivery`/`acknowledgeMailbox`. Routing the\n * scheduler through this function instead would drop the lease semantics.\n *\n * It is kept because it is the clearest single-expression statement of the F-3\n * invariant (\"a cleared record is never live again\") and the seam tests assert it\n * directly (`test/r1-message-channel.test.mjs`, `test/t49-send-dedup-wiring.test.mjs`).\n * Deleting it would remove a cheap, direct guard on a defect that has already escaped\n * once, so it stays — explicitly labelled rather than left as an accidental orphan.\n */\nexport async function readLiveMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey) {\n    return (await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey)).filter((message) => message.tombstone !== true);\n}\n/**\n * Enqueue a first-class interjection REQUEST. It is a normal mailbox record with\n * `kind: 'interjection-request'` and `status: 'pending'`, but it lives in its own\n * QUEUE, never in a member's ordinary inbox: the scheduler packs EVERY unread inbox\n * record verbatim and auto-delivers at the next idle edge (lib/scheduler.ts:223-228,\n * 287-298), so a request in the normal inbox would be delivered and would BYPASS the\n * captain's approval. The payload carries summary + reason + location only; the body\n * follows only after approval.\n *\n * FIELD CONTRACT (repair V1). The mailbox shape REQUIRES a non-empty `content`\n * string, and a record that fails the shape check is invisible to every reader —\n * which used to let a caller create a request that returned `status:'pending'` while\n * nobody could ever see or decide it (a silent failure). `content` is therefore\n * NORMALIZED here rather than left optional: when the caller omits it (or passes an\n * empty string) it is derived, in this fixed priority order, from\n * `summary` -> `reason` -> `location`. `id`, `from` and `ts` are REQUIRED and are\n * rejected loudly when missing, because no fallback can invent an identity or a clock.\n * @param request - the request; `id`/`from`/`ts` required, `content` optional (normalized).\n * @returns the queued request record (always carrying a readable `content`).\n * @throws when a required identity field is missing, naming the field.\n */\nexport async function enqueueInterjection(stateRoot, teamId, request) {\n    for (const field of ['id', 'from', 'ts']) {\n        const value = request?.[field];\n        if (value === undefined || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '')) {\n            throw new Error(`interjection request is missing required field \"${field}\"`);\n        }\n    }\n    // Same fixed priority as the doc above; the first non-empty candidate wins.\n    const rawContent = typeof request.content === 'string' ? ./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-09-17T07-50-36.168Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/agent-references/troubleshooting.md:24:| a plugin change looks green in `--dump-config` but does nothing at runtime (tools missing, routes 404, or the whole tree dead) | `--dump-config` only COMPOSES rows — it never executes plugin code, so it cannot see an apply/schema abort (§4). Reproduce with a boot that MOUNTS the rows in an isolated `DSH_HOME` + sandbox `HOME` (registration instrumentation; `mount-proof.sh` or `bun skills/dsh-qa/scripts/bundle-lifecycle.mjs`) and read the boot log for the apply-crash signatures (`unsupported JSON schema`, `JsonSchemaError`, `plugin tree failed to load`, `failed to apply loader entry`). Measured instance: a `type: ["string","null"]` ARRAY (likewise `["string","array"]`) is REJECTED by this harness and takes the whole tree down; the accepted union spelling is `oneOf: [{type:"string"},{type:"null"}]` (or the `items:` variant), proven by booting. It stayed latent because this release asserts OUTPUT schemas only — never rely on that asymmetry: **a FUTURE instance gets its own scoped change with its own mount proof; do NOT "clean it up" inside an unrelated change** (`mpd_hashline_edit`'s `lines` parameter, proof `evidence/hashline/schema-union-fix/`). |

./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-09-17T07-50-36.168Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/agent-references/troubleshooting.md:31:| a QA/verification run refuses to touch the workmate library (`403 real-home-refused`) | that is the T-43 guard doing its job: `~/.mpd/workmate` is the ONE state root that deliberately lives under the user's HOME, so a boot that sets `DSH_HOME` (isolated/QA shape) but not `HOME=<sandbox>` would write the REAL library. ./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-09-17T07-50-36.168Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/agent-references/troubleshooting.md:40:| a watchdog **WARN** (or an escalating streak) fires for a member that is streaming a very long answer — no tool call is open and `session-watchdog-status` shows the step `OUTSTANDING` | **expected, stated on purpose (contract §1 rule 3) — this is the one place where the watchdog is deliberately conservative instead of silent.** An open step stays `OUTSTANDING` until an `assistant/message` / `assistant/attempt` **commits**; while the model is still delivering a long answer nothing is committed, so a step with no first-token signal honestly stays `OUTSTANDING` and has a clock (a COMPLETED step is `ALIVE` forever and has none). The `agent/assistant-stream` **START frame is the ENRICHMENT** that flips the open `(turn,step)` to `ALIVE` (`noteStreamFrame`, `packages/mpd-team-watchdog-plugin/src/channel.ts`; soft-probed at apply): with it unavailable — or with a harness that never emits a first-token signal — `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` is the BOUND that protects instead of silence. Fix: check the enrichment flag in `session-watchdog-status` and raise `watchdog.warnSilenceMs` when answers legitimately run longer, instead of reading the warn as a wedge. The full asymmetry is also in the package README pair (EN + zh-CN). |

./evidence/extensions/extension-lifecycle/2026-10-06T04-11-18.450Z/scratch-pack/mpd-package/packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:1265:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * P1e (t47): the duplicate window is a CONFIGURED value with its own default, NOT the delivery lease\n * constant it used to borrow. Cleared\n * tombstones are not repeats (their content is empty by construction).\n */\nexport function mailboxDuplicatesFor(existing, message, windowMs) {\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    return (existing ?? The sidecar is what keeps the\n    // operation recoverable, and this guard is what keeps it from being unnecessary.\n    const protectedRecords = inScope.filter((message) => message.deliveredAt === undefined || message.readAt === undefined);\n    const forced = options.force === true;\n    const cleared = forced ? inScope : inScope.filter((message) => !protectedRecords.includes(message));\n    const skipped = forced ? The mailbox shape REQUIRES a non-empty `content`\n * string, and a record that fails the shape check is invisible to every reader —\n * which used to let a caller create a request that returned `status:'pending'` while\n * nobody could ever see or decide it (a silent failure). `content` is therefore\n * NORMALIZED here rather than left optional: when the caller omits it (or passes an\n * empty string) it is derived, in this fixed priority order, from\n * `summary` -> `reason` -> `location`. `id`, `from` and `ts` are REQUIRED and are\n * rejected loudly when missing, because no fallback can invent an identity or a clock.\n * @param request - the request; `id`/`from`/`ts` required, `content` optional (normalized).\n * @returns the queued request record (always carrying a readable `content`).\n * @throws when a required identity field is missing, naming the field.\n */\nexport async function enqueueInterjection(stateRoot, teamId, request) {\n    for (const field of ['id', 'from', 'ts']) {\n        const value = request?.[field];\n        if (value === undefined || (typeof value === 'string' && value.trim() === '')) {\n            throw new Error(`interjection request is missing required field \"${field}\"`);\n        }\n    }\n    // Same fixed priority as the doc above; the first non-empty candidate wins.\n    const rawContent = typeof request.content === 'string' ? ./evidence/team-watchdog/redesign/verify/20260917T040310Z/lane/raw/c-green-reinject-0S9eoa/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:570:        block: "//#region mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/**\n * R1 dormancy fix: make \"captain silence = DENY\" resolve even for a DORMANT team.\n *\n * The scheduler's expiry tick rides a member IDLE EDGE (`kickMember`), so a team that\n * never kicks again leaves a past-due request `pending` and its requester un-notified.\n * This sweep runs at session start, so the next time anyone works in the workspace the\n * past-due rows resolve and their requesters are told.\n *\n * Registered SEPARATELY from the team policy, and deliberately so: expiry is\n * bookkeeping every session needs, not a feature of auto-routing — it must also run\n * when `sessionTeamPolicy.mode` is `off`. Best-effort: a failure degrades to a warning\n * and can never break or reject a session-start step.\n *\n * Boundary (stated, not implied): expiry is evaluated at EVENTS, never by a timer.\n * The events are \"a member became idle\" (scheduler tick) and \"a session started in\n * this workspace\" (this sweep). A workspace nobody ever opens again resolves nothing.\n * @param ctx - the plugin context (needs `on` and `logger`).\n * @param resolved - the resolved plugin config (provides `stateDir`).\n */\nexport function installInterjectionExpirySweep(ctx, resolved) {\n    ctx.on('agent/pre-step', async (payload, next) => {\n        const decision = await next();\n        try {\n            // ONCE PER SESSION, not per step: `agent/pre-step` fires for every step, but\n            // this sweep is a session-start concern (see the sweep guard's declaration).\n            const agentId = payload?.agent?.id;\n            if (typeof agentId === 'string' && agentId !== '') {\n                if (sweptFor.has(agentId))\n                    return decision;\n                sweptFor.add(agentId);\n            }\n            // Resolve the workspace PER CALL from the session that is starting — never a\n            // module-level const and never the process cwd alone (one host serves many\n            // sessions with different workspaces; AGENTS.md §6 State).\n            const workspace = payload?.agent?.session?.header?.cwd ?? process.cwd();\n            const swept = await expireInterjectionsEverywhere(join(workspace, resolved.stateDir));\n            if (swept.expired.length > 0) {\n                ctx.logger.info(`agent-teams: expired ${swept.expired.length} past-due interjection request(s) at session start: ${swept.expired.join(', ')}`);\n            }\n        }\n        catch (error) {\n            ctx.logger.warn(`agent-teams: session-start interjection sweep failed: ${String(error)}`);\n        }\n        return decision;\n    }, { global: true, prepend: true });\n}\n//#endregion mpd-delta interjection-expiry-session-start",
./evidence/team-watchdog/redesign/verify/20260917T040310Z/lane/raw/c-green-reinject-0S9eoa/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:607:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/** Duplicate window for the R1 delivery-idempotency key (from+to+content). */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DELIVERY_LEASE_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. The window is measured on `ts`, and a record\n * that is already delivered/read is still folded — the point is to stop the ACTION,\n * not to shrink the file; nothing is ever physically deleted.\n * @returns the record that now holds the message (new or folded).\n */\nexport async function appendMailboxDeduped(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, message, options = {}) {\n    const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS;\n    const existing = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const key = messageDedupKey(message);\n    const hit = existing.find((candidate) => messageDedupKey(candidate) === key\n        && Math.abs(message.ts - candidate.ts) <= windowMs);\n    if (hit !== undefined) {\n        // R1: the surviving record keeps its OWN delivery/read markers. Dropping them\n        // would clear a live claim (or an acknowledgement) and let a folded duplicate be\n        // delivered again — exactly the duplicate ACTION this primitive exists to stop.\n        const folded = {\n            ...hit,\n            dupCount: (hit.dupCount ?? 1) + 1,\n            ...hit.deliveryClaimedAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveryClaimedAt: hit.deliveryClaimedAt },\n            ...hit.deliveredAt === undefined ? {} : { deliveredAt: hit.deliveredAt },\n            ...hit.readAt === undefined ? {} : { readAt: hit.readAt },\n        };\n        await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [hit.id], () => folded);\n        // `_folded` is a TRANSIENT in-memory marker for the caller (the send boundary must\n        // not re-deliver an already-owned payload). It is never persisted: the record kept\n        // is `folded` alone, so a later fold cannot see a stale marker from an old crash.\n        return { message: { ...folded, _folded: true }, folded: true };\n    }\n    await appendMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 });\n    return { message: { ...message, dupCount: message.dupCount ?? 1 }, folded: false };\n}\n/**\n * Clear a mailbox DOWN TO A WATERMARK: every record with `ts <= watermark` is\n * replaced in place by a tombstone, its original bytes are written to an archive\n * sidecar (`inbox/archive/<agentKey>.<watermark>.jsonl` — the recoverable copy), and\n * ONE audit event describes the operation. There is deliberately NO hard-delete\n * branch: the tombstone keeps the id/ts/from/to so the record stays reviewable, and\n * the sidecar makes the cleared bytes recoverable byte-for-byte.\n * @returns the manifest: tombstoned ids, the sidecar path, and the audit event.\n */\nexport async function clearMailboxToWatermark(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, watermark, options = {}) {\n    const messages = await readMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey);\n    const cleared = messages.filter((message) => message.ts <= watermark && message.tombstone !== true);\n    if (cleared.length === 0) {\n        return { cleared: [], sidecar: undefined, audit: undefined };\n    }\n    const clearedIds = new Set(cleared.map((message) => message.id));\n    // archive-first: the recoverable copy is written AND flushed before the live\n    // file is rewritten, so an interrupted clear always leaves the bytes somewhere.\n    const archiveDir = join(stateRoot, teamId, 'inbox', 'archive');\n    await mkdir(archiveDir, { recursive: true });\n    const sidecar = join(archiveDir, `${sanitizeKey(agentKey)}.${watermark}.jsonl`);\n    await atomicWriteText(sidecar, cleared.map((message) => JSON.stringify(message)).join('\\n') + '\\n');\n    await mutateMailbox(stateRoot, teamId, agentKey, [...clearedIds], (message) => ({\n        id: message.id,\n        from: message.from,\n        to: message.to,\n        content: '',\n        ts: message.ts,\n        tombstone: true,\n        clearedAt: options.now ?? Date.now(),\n        clearedToWatermark: watermark,\n        archivedTo: sidecar,\n        // R1: PRESERVE the read/delivery markers. ./evidence/team-watchdog/redesign/lane/2026-09-17T03-57-04.815Z/raw/c-green-reinject-GBlXX5/lib/mpd-deltas.ts:607:        block: "//#region mpd-delta message-channel-r1 (mpd LOCAL ADAPTATION; re-applied by scripts/patch-agent-teams-fixes.mjs)\n/** Duplicate window for the R1 delivery-idempotency key (from+to+content). */\nexport const MAILBOX_DEDUP_WINDOW_MS = MAILBOX_DELIVERY_LEASE_MS;\n/** Interjection requests still unanswered after this are DENIED by default. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_TTL_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;\n/** Lane that holds interjection REQUESTS awaiting the captain's decision. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_QUEUE = 'interjections';\n/** Message kind marking a first-class interjection request. */\nexport const INTERJECTION_KIND = 'interjection-request';\n/** The R1 delivery-idempotency key: sender + recipient + content. */\nexport function messageDedupKey(message) {\n    return `${message.from}\\u0000${message.to}\\u0000${message.content}`;\n}\n/**\n * Fold one message into the mailbox for DELIVERY idempotency: when the same\n * (from,to,content) was appended inside the window, the existing record's\n * `dupCount` is incremented and NO second record is written, so a redelivery can\n * never make the recipient act twice. ./evidence/team-watchdog/design/DESIGN.md:43:**[M] Tool stamps are POST.** The adapter exposes `onPostToolExecute` (`packages/mpd-dsh-adapter-plugin/src/index.ts:274`, impl `:535`) and `executeTool`/`toolRuntime().execute` (`:279`, impl `:564`), plus the read-only `guardTool` (`:273`, impl `:529`). `guardTool`'s contract is "read only, never mutate" (AGENTS.md §6), so a heartbeat MUST NOT be written there. A pre-dispatch stamp therefore needs the declared adapter extension to `tools/execute` (§5-H1b / W-9) and is **NOT-CLAIMED for v1**; AC-2 asserts the POST stamp only.
./evidence/team-watchdog/design/DESIGN.md:54:**[M] Honest bound on the step stamp.** `agent/pre-step` is dispatched by the loop *before* the model call for that step, so a `step` stamp means "a step began", not "the model answered". A stream that stalls mid-step therefore still shows a recent `step` stamp — the exact wedge this wave exists for. **The design does not pretend otherwise:** staleness is computed from the **newest stamp of ANY kind**, and the incident's symptom (a member silent for ~20 minutes) is caught because no further `pre-step` fires either once the turn is wedged before its next step. The residual blind spot — a step that begins and its model call then hangs forever — is stated in AC-15's terms as a known false-negative window of one step, and it is why the `assistant-stream` frame event is listed as an optional refinement in §9 rather than claimed.
./evidence/team-watchdog/design/DESIGN.md:58:**[D] A per-member append-only heartbeat file beside the team state, NOT inside `team.json`.** `packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/state.js` keeps **sole ownership of `team.json`** (`D§d`, and the plan's §5-H2b requires the same separation for the hold); writing heartbeats into it would create a second writer on an adopted file's byte surface and a write loop under a per-step cadence.

./evidence/team-watchdog/design/DESIGN.md:168:**[D] Tool-boundary guards: ADDITIVE, and v1 can ship without them.** §5-H2b requires guards because a member already holding an attempt can still call `agent_teams_update_task` while the team is held. **[M] The guard sites today** are `tools.js:111` (plan-edit refusal), `:228` (captain-path halted read), `:1139` (create_task), `:1991` (wake/send), and **`agent_teams_claim_task` has NO halted guard** (`:1343`).
